references.text: The same law shall apply to the native-born and to the foreigner living among you—a parallel principle of one law for all.
The assembly shall have one statute, both for you and for the foreigner living among you—the same legal standard for natives and foreigners.
One law shall apply to the one who sins unintentionally, both for the native-born and for the foreigner.
The same regulation shall apply to the foreigner as to the native-born when it comes to celebrating Passover.
Prohibition against oppressing or mistreating the foreigner, with the reasoning that the Israelites themselves were foreigners in Egypt.
Command to love the foreigner as yourself and not wrong him, because the Israelites themselves were foreigners in Egypt.
Judges shall judge fairly between a man and his brother and the foreigner—no partiality toward any person.
You shall not pervert justice for the foreigner or the fatherless—justice for all.
In Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek—a New Testament principle of equality reflecting God's righteousness for all.
In Christ there is no Greek and Jew, circumcised and uncircumcised—all are equal before God.
